data.title: SOCIA-$\nabla$: Textual Gradient Meets Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Simulator Generation
data.description:
arXiv:2505.12006v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we present SOCIA-$
abla$, a diagnosis-driven multi-agent framework for automated simulator-code construction. SOCIA-$
abla$ iteratively refines executable simulator code within a textual computation graph, where LLM-driven agents synthesize, execute, evaluate, diagnose, and repair simulators. A grounded simulator blueprint attributes behavioral residuals to candidate mechanisms and their spatial or interaction contexts, which are then converted into localized textual repair signals with history-aware memory and constraint projection. We evaluate SOCIA-$
abla$ on the real-world LLMob personal-mobility benchmark and a controlled semi-synthetic geo-social mask-adoption benchmark. Across in-distribution simulation, out-of-distribution what-if generation, and geo-social diffusion, SOCIA-$
abla$ achieves the strongest overall simulator fidelity. SOCIA-$
abla$'s code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/cruiseresearchgroup/SOCIA-Nabla.
data.author: Yuncheng Hua, Sion Weatherhead, Mehdi Jafari, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim
